results.note: Every number matches. Abstract › Methods and Search Strategy: eight databases plus ClinicalTrials.gov and grey literature, inception to November 2018, four amphetamine keywords only. Table 2: six trials, arms 36/44, 21/21, 27/26, 19/18, 22/22 and 29/29 (sum 314), 25 days to 8 weeks, the placebo-controlled trial 8 weeks in Malaysia, GRADE R+ for all six (the note calls the rating low). Synthesis of Results, 1st paragraph: all trials excluded DSM-IV schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder. 'Nothing pooled' is not at the listed places (the abstract says results were synthesized 'qualitatively and quantitatively'); it is stated in Assessment of Heterogeneity and Data Synthesis and Analysis, now added to the locator. The editors' comparison was checked against card sc_srisurapanont_2021: the network's six head-to-head trials include all five here (Verachai, Wang 2016, Farnia, Samiei, Leelahanaj). Role supports: right.
results.corrected_locator: Abstract › Methods; Materials and Methods › Search Strategy; Materials and Methods › Assessment of Heterogeneity; Materials and Methods › Data Synthesis and Analysis; Results › Description of Studies; Results › Synthesis of Results, 1st paragraph; Table 2

results.note: Numbers match Table 3 (Wang row: agitation 52.4 vs 19.0, akathisia 61.9 vs 28.60, discontinuation 33 vs 0; Leelahanaj row: completers 93.1 vs 65.5) and the text (p < 0.005; CGI-S 2 and 2.1; haloperidol more extrapyramidal syndrome). Two fixes: the review gives the CGI-S of 2 vs 2.1 without a time point, so 'at the end' is dropped; and the akathisia and agitation on aripiprazole against placebo are in the Side Effects subsection 'Aripiprazole, Placebo', which the locator did not list. Conclusions, 2nd paragraph, holds the efficacy conclusion with the self-limited caveat. The SMD sentence restates the card's analysis, which I confirmed (four intervals symmetric only with lost minus signs; no comparison or direction stated). Role qualifies: right.

results.corrected_extracted: In the placebo-controlled trial, symptoms fell more on aripiprazole than on placebo (p < 0.005 in the text, p < 0.05 in Table 3), with mean CGI-S 2 on aripiprazole and 2.1 on placebo (time point not stated), and more akathisia and agitation on aripiprazole. In the 42-participant aripiprazole–risperidone trial: agitation 52.4% vs 19.0%, akathisia 61.9% vs 28.6%, discontinuation 33% vs 0%; in the olanzapine–haloperidol trial: completers 93.1% vs 65.5%, more extrapyramidal symptoms on haloperidol. The review's conclusion that antipsychotics are efficacious rests on improvement within each arm, and its per-trial SMDs (Table 3) do not state what they compare and partly lack minus signs (study card sc_fluyau_2019, reporting issues 1 to 3).
